next.name: GOLD LOCUST
next.headline: GOLD LOCUST: the Carbanak and FIN7 name cluster, seen in malspam and a ransomware case
next.in_short: Secureworks tracks GOLD LOCUST under several names, including FIN7 and Carbanak. Malwarebytes attributes a malspam campaign that dropped JSSLoader to FIN7. IBM X-Force links a Carbanak backdoor to a ransomware case.

sentences.t: Secureworks tracks this actor as GOLD LOCUST.
The catalogue lists these aliases: Anunak, Carbanak, Carbon Spider, FIN7 and Silicon.
Carbanak is the one tool named in the catalogue record.
Malwarebytes Threat Intelligence attributes a late-June malspam campaign to FIN7.
Malwarebytes says the campaign dropped JSSLoader, a rewrite of the loader with expanded capabilities, including data exfiltration.
It also dropped a secondary payload written in .NET.
Malwarebytes notes an earlier component used by this group, delivered in XLL format, which others had already described.
Malwarebytes published its account of the late-June campaign on August 15, 2022.
IBM Security X-Force investigated a Carbanak backdoor that was associated with a Sodinokibi ransomware attack.
IBM X-Force concludes that ITG14 is at least one affiliate group that contracts with Sodinokibi ransomware-as-a-service providers.
The report's Carbanak link rests on the similarity of the backdoor to ITG14's tools.
Treat unexpected email attachments with caution, and keep an eye on how remote access to your network is secured.
